stem: Damini forms values with the four fixed numbers $9$, $6$, $4$, and $1$ by writing $9\pm 6\pm 4\pm 1$ and choosing each sign independently.

parts.text: Which claim correctly decides whether changing the signs can change the odd/even parity of the value?

options.text: Yes: each sign change flips the parity of the value.
No: every choice of signs gives a value with the same parity.
Only the sign in front of $9$ can change the parity.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Changing one sign alters the value by twice that number, which is even, so the parity never changes. For these four numbers the common parity is even.

teacher.key_rationale: A sign flip changes the value by ±2 times a term (even). All eight sign patterns therefore share one parity; here 9+6+4+1=20 is even.
